messages.subject_clean: "Java heap space" Error when trying to find the values of a given key in map files
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

I'm trying to get the values associated with a given key in map files on the HDFS through the following command:
x <- rhmapfile(location_on_hdfs)       # line 1
x[[key]]                                          # line 2

And I'm doing this kind of queries lots of times and on different directories of map files on HDFS in the same R session, which means both line 1 and line 2 are called multiple times.

After a few runs, I'm getting the "Java heap space" errors:

Error in .jcall("RJavaTools", "Ljava/lang/Object;", "invokeMethod", cl, :
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space

And I won't be able to query a given key any more unless I quit R and restart R.

Could someone provide some insight on this?
When performing such queries of a given key, is the NameNode reads in all the index files into memory?  And since I'm doing it multiple times with different directories, some of which can contain index files of large size (a few hundreds of MB), the NameNode eventually runs out of memory?

Another related question is:
can I perform such queries of given keys inside a map-reduce job?

The reason I want to do all these is because I now have graph-like data and I want to reach a node's neighbors and the neighbors' neighbors.  I'm storing a node's name as the key, the node's information and all its neighbor's id as the value.  I want to be able to perform breadth-first search to a certain degrees.  Any thought on this?

Thanks.  Any thoughts and comments are greatly appreciated.

Cheers

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the quick response.

I'll repeat the crashing operation with rhcacheStats and let you know the results.

The default heap space is 512MB, and I'll run it with increased heap space to see if this solves the problem.
> options("java.parameters")
$java.parameters
[1] "-Xmx512m"

I want to first comment on your last comment.  I didn't make myself clear when I asked the second question: besides looking for neighbors and neighbors' neighbors in a breadth-first search fashion, we could also be looking for (1) more than depth=2 related nodes, and (2) since this is a directed graph, we'd like to follow a path and search in a depth-first fashion as well.
Storing neighbors' information and their neighbors information has two down sides:
1. the data gets replicated a few times.  this is not a big issue if depth=2, but it grows very fast with depth.
2. this pre-defines the depth we can go and thus makes it impossible to perform a depth-first search.

I'm guessing Rhipe or Hadoop in general is not designed for handling graph data, but we are now dealing with a few GB of bitcoin data and graph models seems to be appropriate.  We probably just need to perform breadth-first and/or depth-first search for a few nodes, and we can get away by doing them sequentially in a regular R session.  But I just want to know if it is all possible to perform such searches on a larger scale.  And that's why I wanted to perform search in a map-reduce job.

Cheers

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Those warnings appear because rhipe tries to autmatically detect variables you're referring to and copy them from the workspace.
E.g.
DO_F = function(i) runif(i)

rhwatch(map= function(key,value){
    rhcollect(key, DO_F(value)
}, reduce.....)

then RHIPE will automatically detect your code refers to DO_F and copy it along with everything else. The logic is not perfect and so it sees in reduce$reduce
that collect is being referred to and yet can't find it the workspace. This despite that collect is initialized to NULL in reduce$pre

If you want to avoid these warnings, do

copyObjects =rhoptions()$copyObjects
copyObjects$auto= FALSE
rhoptions(copyObjects=copyObjects)

Then RHIPE will not automatically copy objects (it's algorithm is not the ... best) but instead you will have to manuall pass them as in
rhwatch(..., param=list(DO_F = DO_F)...

Hello,

I read in passing an issue with "total order sorting" in RHIPE.
I.e how do i sort a data set by a key into N files, so that all keys in Ni are less than all the keys
in Nj (for j>i) and all keys inside Ni are sorted.

Note, this works for integer and string keys before version 0.72.1-2.
0.72-1.2 fixes the bug for numeric vectors: hence the code below will only work for
0.72-1.2 ( http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipebin/Rhipe_0.73.1-2.tar.gz )

The following code creates a dataset where the keys are between 0 and 1

map <- function(a,b)
  for(i in 1:1000)
   rhcollect(runif(1),1)
m <- rhwatch(map=map, reduce=0, input=c(1000,3),read=FALSE)

The following code will sort it into 10 files (10 reducers) the ranges in each
file defined by 'intervals'. Note how the map emits a 'reduceBucket' which sends the keys to the
correct partitioner. The reduce code then drops this 'reduceBucket' key.

intervals <- seq(0,1,length=10)

mapsort <- expression({
  whichReducer <- findInterval( unlist(map.keys), intervals)
  mapply(function(reduceBucket, key,value){
    rhcollect(c(reduceBucket,key), value)
  }, whichReducer, map.keys,map.values,SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
})

reducer <- expression(
    reduce = {
      lapply(reduce.values, function(v) rhcollect(reduce.key[2], v))
    })

sorter <- rhwatch(map=mapsort, reduce=reducer, input=m
                  ,orderby='numeric'
                  ,partitioner=list(type='numeric',lims=1)
                  ,mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks = length(intervals))
                  ,read=FALSE)

          Cheers
          Saptarshi

  whichReducer <- findInterval( unlist(map.keys), intervals)
  mapply(function(reduceBucket, key,value){

  }, whichReducer, map.keys,map.values,SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
})
intervals <- seq(0,1,length=50)

    reduce = {

## For demonstration, keep the bucket (so that we can confirm sorting took place
## and drop that 'magnified discretized key'
      lapply(reduce.values, function(v) rhcollect(c(reduce.key[1],v[[1]]), v[[2]]))
    })

sorter <- rhwatch(map=mapsort, reduce=reducer, input=m

                  ,orderby='integer'
                  ,partitioner=list(type='integer',lims=1)
                  ,mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks = length(intervals)-2) ## the first and last will never have values in them
                  ,read=FALSE)

## Confirm
       mu <- lapply(rhls(sorter)$file[grepl("part",rhls(sorter)$file)],function(i){
         a <- rhread(i)
         j <- unlist(lapply(a,function(r) r[[1]][[2]]))
         list( unlist(lapply(a,function(r) r[[1]][[1]]))[[1]], range(j))
